classification.difficultyReason: Translate nonconcurrent and nonparallel into three pairwise intersections at distinct points, then draw an arrangement satisfying both constraints.

content.prompt: Draw three lines that are not concurrent and so that no two of the lines are parallel.

answer.short: For example, three extended lines forming a triangle.
answer.worked: Draw two intersecting lines. Draw a third line crossing both at separate points, away from their intersection. The three lines meet pairwise at three distinct points, so they are not concurrent and no pair is parallel.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2; answer evidence on teacher PDF page 46, printed page 421
spec.description: Two crossing oblique lines and a horizontal line below their crossing; every line extends beyond its intersections.
spec.mathematics: Three distinct pairwise intersections; no parallel pair and no common intersection of all three lines.
spec.answerVisibility: Example construction appears only in answer editions.
